> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 48 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0e004ed7e0accd9eff51823b622b1dfe7c548b2b` — the merge of head `1b5c8eef84dfeb09fbd6be44435f73f5ae85ab04` into base `57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0e004ed7e0accd9eff51823b622b1dfe7c548b2b && git checkout 0e004ed7e0accd9eff51823b622b1dfe7c548b2b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc 1b5c8eef84dfeb09fbd6be44435f73f5ae85ab04 && git checkout -B drift-repro 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc && git merge --no-ff 1b5c8eef84dfeb09fbd6be44435f73f5ae85ab04

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57c51aab4d2f63293676e9412daed8a5fc54c1bc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5a8a02333cb35c9c4aa77e0656e65b54b9f69263`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts + packages/rest/src/email-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/transports/smtp.ts, packages/rest/src/email-send-door-bounds.test.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.test.ts, .changeset/harden-rest-email-send-door.md

Inputs read: PR #27469 body, file list (12 files), net diff vs `main` at the head, all 2 PR comments (docs-drift advisory; triage claim), and the 50 check-runs on the head: 41 `success`, 9 `skipped` (opt-in / matrix placeholders), 0 pending, 0 failure. No card exists: the PR body says it was sent straight to a dev seat with no tracking issue, and no comment names one.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec`:** `IEmailService` gains an optional `getDefaultFrom?(): EmailAddress | undefined`. Additive, implementer-optional, consumer-nullable. Right. `check:api-surface` is among the green Lint gates; the `api-surface/contracts.json` baseline lists exports, not members, so no baseline moves. Right.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/rest`:** two new exports from `email-routes.ts` (`EMAIL_SEND_CAPABILITY`, `SENDER_HEADER_NAMES`). The package entry does not re-export `email-routes.ts` (module header, confirmed on the head), so the published surface of `@objectstack/rest` does not move. Right.
- **Accept set of `POST {base}/email/send` (both mounts, unscoped and environment-scoped):** narrowed on three axes. (1) An authenticated caller without `manage_platform_settings` in the resolved context's `systemPermissions` is refused 403 before the provider lookup; an absent or non-array `systemPermissions` reads as the empty set. Fails closed; same field the federation door (`external-datasource-routes.ts`) and the package door read, populated by `core/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`. Right. (2) `sentBy` differing from `String(context.userId)` is refused; the forwarded `sentBy` is always the caller. Right. (3) A caller `from` is admitted only when its bare lower-cased address equals the configured sender's, and the forwarded value is the configured object, never the caller's text; absent accessor or unconfigured sender refuses a caller `from`. Right, and airtight for the `from` field itself.
- **Capability choice:** `manage_platform_settings` is a declared platform capability (`spec/security/capabilities.ts`, `PLATFORM_ADMIN` set in `eval-user.zod.ts`). It is the `readPermission`/`writePermission` of the `mail` settings manifest (`service-settings/src/manifests/mail.manifest.ts:52-53`) and the object-level `requiredPermissions` of `sys_identity_email`. On `sys_email` it gates the two body columns (`body_text`/`body_html`), not the row: the docblock's "the `sys_email` log is gated on it" is right for the bodies only. Precision, not a defect.
- **Envelope:** the three refusals use the nested `{ error: { code, message } }` shape `enforceAuth` writes; the 501/400 in the same handler keep their pre-existing flat shape. `check:route-envelope` is green on the head. Right.
- **Server-internal callers unchanged:** flows, notifications, auth mail and the messaging channel call `IEmailService.send` directly; the diff touches only the HTTP handler. Right.
- **Wrong:** the sender-header clause of bound 3 does not hold for every shape the wire can carry (④, must-fix 1).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `patch` on `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/client`; `Metadata-protocol: none`. Under ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) `none` takes `patch` on every entry, and the spec precedent for this exact kind of change (`fccbd9d`, `IEmailService.isConfigured()`) shipped as a Patch Change. Level: right. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green.
- **`Clause-②: no` is wrong against the diff.** The diff adds an optional member to the published `IEmailService` contract, which is a widening of a public surface; the repo's own declaration for the identical move on the identical interface reads `Clause-②: yes (widening: an optional member on IEmailService)` (`fccbd9d`, spec CHANGELOG). The gate comment keeps Clause-②'s meaning as "does this diff widen or narrow a published accept set or public surface"; a `no` over an added contract member contradicts it. Must-fix 2: the PR body and changeset carry `Clause-②: yes`, with the arm the maintainer rules (below).
- **Arm (escalated, not graded):** the door now refuses callers and bodies it admitted. Precedent is split: `d9d7edd` (ADR-0069 gate added to doors that answered a held session) declared `no (narrowing)` with a BREAKING banner and an `adr-0087:` marker; `7a606a9` and `454bbb6` (adding `manage_platform_settings` to existing `/meta` doors) declared a bare `no`. If the maintainer reads this as the former, the line is `yes (narrowing)`, the changeset gains the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition marker (the migration paragraph is already present). The reviewer does not decide this; the maintainer does.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag, capability choice (org admins cannot send):** answered. The capability matches who may configure the transport and read the identity log today; a dedicated send capability is a `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` addition and belongs to a decision, not this PR. Escalated to the maintainer as a follow-up decision; no change owed here.
- **Dev flag, per-send display name lost:** answered, by design under bound 3 (the configured object is forwarded verbatim). No change owed.
- **Dev flag, `organizationId` / `identityMail` pass through unbounded:** answered as acceptable for this head because the admitted caller is platform-scoped, but it stays open: a holder can stamp any `organization_id` on the `sys_email` row or route a message into `sys_identity_email`. Escalated for a follow-up card.
- **Not flagged by the dev, raised here, `replyTo` is unbounded:** a caller may direct replies to any address. Reply-To is not a sender claim and the PR does not claim to bound it; recorded as an open question for the same follow-up, not a defect of this change.
- **Not flagged by the dev, raised here, `headers` shape:** see ④ must-fix 1.
- No `open_questions` block exists on the PR or a card.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts` (hits).** Judged against the ADR it cites (ADR-0124, the server is the enforcement point) and its first consumer, the REST door.

- The member is optional, zero-argument, and its docblock binds the consumer to read absence as UNKNOWN and refuse a caller-chosen `from`. The first consumer does exactly that: `typeof emailService.getDefaultFrom === 'function' ? ... : undefined`, then `!configuredAddress` refuses. The plugin-email implementation reads `this.options.defaultFrom` live, so it follows `setDefaultFrom` from the `mail` namespace; pinned in `email-service.test.ts` (plugin-email). The contract holds against both. No finding on the member itself.
- **Should-fix (parity):** `packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.test.ts` pins the sibling optional member `isConfigured` at compile time (absent assignable; wrong return type refused). No equivalent pin is added for `getDefaultFrom`. The REST bounds test's `Partial` of `IEmailService` double type-checks the member indirectly, so the shape is not unpinned, but the spec's own contract test is where the repo pins this interface.

**Cited code, read to judge the scenario the member is accepted against (the door's refusals fail closed):**

- Bound 1 fails closed on every shape of `systemPermissions` (absent, non-array, array without the name). Bound 2 fails closed (strict inequality against the stringified caller id). Bound 3's `from` clause fails closed on every shape of `from` (`null`, empty, array, object without `address`, string with a trailing angle-bracket address that differs, string with the address placed anywhere but the end): `addressOf` yields `undefined` or a non-matching string, and the forwarded value is the configured object regardless. These hold.
- **Must-fix 1: the sender-header clause of bound 3 does not hold for every `headers` shape the wire can carry.** The name scan and the transport do not read the same container, so a reserved sender header can still reach the message on the inline path. ⛔ The mechanism is withheld from GitHub (maintainer rule on security findings, #27382), and the triage seat has handed it to the maintainer. **Fix:** before the name scan, refuse (403, the same envelope) any `headers` that is not a plain object whose every value is a string, or normalize it to that shape and scan the result, so the check and the transport read one container. **Pin:** one case in `email-send-door-bounds.test.ts` posting a `headers` value outside that shape from an entitled caller, asserting 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` and that `send` is never called; and one asserting that a record with a non-string value is refused or coerced before `send`.
- The 17-case bounds test otherwise covers both sides of each bound through the real Hono transport, proves the service is never called on refusal, and proves the forwarded `from` is the configured object. The two existing email-door suites grant the capability only to measure what lies past the gate, which is the right repair. The ablation account in the PR body is not relied on; the tree is.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1b5c8eef84dfeb09fbd6be44435f73f5ae85ab04`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts + packages/rest/src/email-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/email-send-door-bounds.test.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/transports/smtp.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/transports/smtp.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, .changeset/harden-rest-email-send-door.md

Inputs read: PR #27469 body, file list (15 files), net diff vs `main` at the head, all 3 PR comments (docs-drift advisory; the prior FAIL record on `5a8a0233`; triage's claim on this head), and the 50 check-runs on the head: 41 `success`, 9 `skipped` (matrix placeholders and opt-in lanes), 0 pending, 0 failure. No card exists: the PR body says the work went straight to a dev seat, and no comment names one. This is a re-review on a moved head; the delta section at the end verifies every prior finding.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec`:** `IEmailService` gains the optional `getDefaultFrom?(): EmailAddress | undefined`. Additive, implementer-optional, consumer-nullable; the `api-surface/contracts.json` baseline lists exports, not members, so nothing moves there and `check:api-surface` (Lint & Repo Gates) is green. Right.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/rest`:** `email-routes.ts` exports `EMAIL_SEND_CAPABILITY` and `SENDER_HEADER_NAMES`; `packages/rest/src/index.ts` on this head does not re-export the module, so the published surface of the package does not move. Right.
- **Behaviour, `@objectstack/plugin-email` (every sender, not only the door):** `SmtpTransport.send` now hands nodemailer custom headers as an explicit list of name/value entries, one per key of the message's headers map, in key order; `smtp.test.ts` pins the list and its order. For a well-formed map this is the same set of header fields on the wire; the Postmark and Resend transports already consume the map their own way and are unchanged. Right.
- **Accept set of `POST {base}/email/send` (both mounts):** narrowed on four axes, each refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` in the nested envelope before the service is called. (1) Caller must hold `manage_platform_settings` in the resolved `systemPermissions`; absent or non-array reads as the empty set; judged before the provider lookup. Right. (2) `sentBy` must be absent or the caller; the forwarded value is always the caller. Right. (3) A caller `from` is admitted only when its bare lower-cased address equals the configured sender's, and the configured object is forwarded in its place; an absent accessor or unconfigured sender refuses a caller `from`. `headers` is admitted in exactly one shape: a plain object (null or `Object.prototype` prototype, never an array) whose every key passes the RFC 5322 field-name grammar (printable US-ASCII, no colon) and whose every value is a string without CR or LF, and no key lower-cases to `from`, `sender` or `return-path`. Right. (4) `organizationId` must be absent or equal the caller's vetted `tenantId`; a caller with no active organization may not name one; `identityMail` must be absent or `false`; the forwarded message strips both caller fields and stamps the vetted organization when there is one. Right.
- **Where bound 4's organization comes from:** `context.tenantId`, the field `resolveAuthzContext` (core) sets from an API key's vetted principal or from the session claim after `vetOrganizationClaim` — a claim for an organization the caller no longer belongs to is dropped and `ctx.tenantId` deleted, so the door reads `undefined` and refuses a body that names one. `meta-item-read-gate.ts`'s `metaCallerOrganizationId` reads the same field; one source, as the module header says. The service stamps the forwarded value verbatim onto `sys_email.organization_id` and reads no other organization. Right.
- **Fail-closed on odd values:** `organizationId: null`, `identityMail: null`, `headers: null` and `from: null` are each refused (the `!== undefined` guards admit only absence). Right.

- **Server-internal callers unchanged:** flows, notifications, auth mail and the messaging channel call `IEmailService.send` directly; only the HTTP handler and the SMTP header hand-off changed. Right.
- **Still passed through unbounded:** `replyTo` (the module header now says so and why), `relatedObject`, `relatedId`, `cc`, `bcc`, `attachments`. None is a sender, attribution or tenant claim; see ③.
- **Wrong:** the PR body's `Clause-②` declaration (② below).

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** (`.changeset/harden-rest-email-send-door.md`): `patch` on `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/client`; title `fix(rest)!: …`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the reasoning for both halves (the door's accept-set narrowing; the optional member's widening, the `isConfigured()` precedent); `Metadata-protocol: none`; the adr-0087 HTML-comment marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its facts; the `**BREAKING**` banner; and a "What changes for you" migration paragraph. Under ruling A `none` takes `patch` on every entry and a non-protocol narrowing keeps its banner and disposition at `patch`; `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads the `narrowing` arm from the changeset and found its marker (Lint & Repo Gates green). Level right, arm right, disposition right.
- **Must-fix 1 (carried from the prior record's must-fix 2, half resolved): the PR body still declares `Clause-②: no`.** Line 1 of the body on this head reads `Clause-②: no`, with no arm, while the changeset in the same PR reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. AGENTS.md §3 requires the declaration on both carriers; the in-CI semver gate (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, "ONE carrier: the fixed `Clause-②:` line in the PR body") reads the body alone and therefore records this PR as neither widening nor breaking, which is the exact condition the direction arm was ruled in to end (#16421: a narrowing shipping with every gate green). No gate cross-checks the two carriers, so both are green while they contradict each other. **Fix:** the PR body's line 1 reads `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, byte-identical in value and arm to the changeset's; `Metadata-protocol: none` stays. A body edit does not move the head; `pr-automation.yml` re-runs Check Changeset on `edited`, and `patch` under `none` keeps it green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag, capability choice (organization administrators cannot send):** answered; the capability is the one that configures the transport and reads the identity log; a dedicated send capability is a `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` decision, not this PR. Escalated to the maintainer as a follow-up decision; no change owed here.
- **Dev flag, per-send display name lost:** answered by design under bound 3; no change owed.
- **Dev flag, `organizationId` / `identityMail` "not bounded here":** superseded by this head, which bounds both (bound 4). The flag survives only in the stale PR body (should-fix 1).
- **Raised in the prior record, `replyTo` unbounded:** answered on this head in the module header, the changeset, the docs and the client JSDoc: it is a caller-supplied Reply-To and makes no sender claim. Stays an open question for the follow-up card, not a defect.
